Logit-Lens Results & How Should We Define Perception, and What Tools Do We Use to Analyze It
Alina Liu · Progress update, week of September 29, 2026
1.1 Run 2 (September 30)
50 episodes on one V100: 42 succeeded = 84.0%
One step of an episode
1. Into OpenVLA: one camera image (rotated, resized and center-cropped to 224 × 224, as in OpenVLA's own evaluation) and the instruction, in the prompt “In: What action should the robot take to <instruction>? Out:”.
2. Out of OpenVLA: 7 tokens, one per action part (x, y, z, roll, pitch, yaw, gripper), each one of 256 bins. They become one movement, sent to the simulator, which renders the next image.
3. Where the logit lens runs: after every layer (input + 32 layers), at the position that writes each of the 7 tokens. That layer's numbers go through the model's final norm and output layer, keeping only the 256 bin scores.
4. What is kept: for each token at each layer, the top bin. Also the 7 bins the model chose, the movement sent, and the gripper and object positions. Per episode: success and number of steps.
Repeated up to 220 steps per episode, stopping at success.

2.1 How to read the charts
Measured for each of the 7 action parts, at each layer, at every step
Measure
What it means in words
Exact agreement
Did this layer pick exactly the bin the model finally outputs? Yes or no, shown as % of steps.
Distance
How close did it get? The gap between this layer's bin and the final bin, as % of that part's range (1 bin ≈ 0.4%).
Baseline (dashed line)
A fake layer that always says the bin the model outputs most often for that part. Its score is the line a real layer must beat to show it knows anything.
Exact vs. distance, an example
Final x bin = 120. Layer 20 picks 121, layer 10 picks 200.
Exact: both are misses. Distance: layer 20 is 1 bin off (0.4%), layer 10 is 80 bins off (31%). Distance shows layer 20 is nearly there.
Why the baseline matters
Some answers are very common. “Close” is the gripper's output on 53% of steps, “no roll” on 50%; x's most common bin only 21%.
So a gripper layer at 50% knows nothing yet. On the distance chart, the line is how far that same constant guess is from the final bin.
3
2.2 Exact agreement: the action appears late
How often each layer already picks the final bin, per action part
Movement (x, y, z, roll, pitch, yaw): near 0% up to layer 16. Beats the baseline only at layers 25–28.
Gripper: uses only 2 of the 256 bins (open, close), so it is a yes/no choice. Beats its baseline at layer 19, 83% by layer 24.
Tasks differ: at layer 28, x matches on 18–31% of steps depending on the task. The whole band stays low until the last layers.
4
2.3 Distance: roughly right comes before exactly right
How far each layer's bin is from the final bin (lower = closer)
Layers 1–16: every part is 23–44% of its range away from the answer: no better than a fixed guess.
Closer before exact: on distance, x and y beat the baseline at layer 24 and z at 18, before they match exactly (25–28).
Gripper is under 1% away by layer 28.

3.1 Perception: Looking at Image Patch Positions
Same lens, same frozen model: only where it reads and which words it may pick change
Run 2 (done): action lens. When does the action appear?
Image + instruction
→
Vision + projector → 256 image tokens
→
Llama-2 layers 1–32
→
Read at the position writing each of the 7 action tokens
→
Final norm rescales the 4096 numbers
→
Output layer a score for all 32,064 entries
→
Keep the 256 action bins
Run 3 (proposed): perception lens. What does each patch show, and where?
Image + instruction
→
Vision + projector → 256 image tokens
→
Llama-2 layers 1–32
→
Read at (changed) each of the 256 image-patch positions
→
Final norm same
→
Output layer OpenVLA's, or Prismatic's as a fallback
→
Keep (changed) the ~31,700 text words, not the action bins
Definition: perception at layer k = the patch over an object decodes to that object's name (“bowl”) at layer k. The word gives what; the patch's place in the 16 × 16 grid gives where.

Mostly fragments. A patch's top word is usually a word piece or foreign token. “regularly” is the top word on ~70 of 256 patches at layers 20–24: a default, not a perception.
Some real scene words, layers 20–28. “table” is the top word for some patch on 84–99% of steps; “floor” ranks 2.
“Bowl” is not found: no better than the control words. Layer 32 is junk.
Can OpenVLA's output layer still produce words? Partly: surface words (table, floor), not the object.
